# First, identify rows where laps > 75
above_75 = df[df['laps'] > 75]

# For these rows, check if the 'time / retired' column contains a time (i.e., a colon indicating a time format) or a retirement reason (no colon).
# A time entry typically contains a colon (e.g., "1:47:35.5", "+ 20.9", "+ 1 lap", "+ 2 laps", "+ 4 laps").
# A retirement reason does not contain a colon (e.g., "engine", "gearbox", "accident", etc.).
# We'll check if the string contains a colon to determine if it's a time.
has_time = above_75['time / retired'].str.contains(':', na=False)

# Count how many drivers above 75 laps have a retirement reason (i.e., no time listed)
no_time_count = (~has_time).sum()

# The claim says: "any driver above 75 laps care trouble of some kind thus no time listed"
# This means: there exists at least one driver with laps > 75 whose 'time / retired' is not a time (i.e., a retirement reason).
# So we check if no_time_count > 0
answer = (no_time_count > 0)
